title: Halle Berry
wiki_lead:
Halle Maria Berry (born Maria Halle Berry; August 14, 1966) is an American actress. She began her career as a model and beauty contestant, becoming Miss Ohio USA in 1986, finishing as first runner-up at Miss USA 1986, and placing sixth at Miss World 1986. Her early film roles include Boomerang (1992), The Flintstones (1994) and Bulworth (1998). She produced and starred in the television film Introducing Dorothy Dandridge (1999), for which she won a Primetime Emmy Award and a Golden Globe Award.
Berry won the Academy Award for Best Actress for her portrayal of a struggling widow in the romantic drama Monster's Ball (2001). She played Storm in the X-Men film series (2000–2014), a villain in Swordfish (2001), the Bond girl Jinx in Die Another Day (2002), a psychiatrist in Gothika (2003), and Catwoman in Catwoman (2004). She also appeared in Perfect Stranger (2007), Cloud Atlas (2012) and The Call (2013), Kingsman: The Golden Circle (2017) and John Wick: Chapter 3 – Parabellum (2019).
Berry produced the television film Lackawanna Blues (2005), and subsequently produced several projects in which she also performed, including the film Frankie & Alice (2010) and the CBS science fiction series Extant (2014–2015). In 2014, Berry launched the production company 606 Films. In 2020, she made her directorial debut with the Netflix drama Bruised. She has been a Revlon spokesmodel since 1996. She was formerly married to baseball player David Justice, singer-songwriter Eric Benét, and actor Olivier Martinez. Berry shares one child with Martinez and another with her former partner Gabriel Aubry.

Early life
Maria Halle Berry was born on August 14, 1966 in Cleveland, Ohio. Her mother is Judith Ann (née Hawkins), a first generation American whose own mother was from Liverpool. Her father is Jerome Jesse Berry, an African-American man who died in 2003. Berry's mother worked as a psychiatric nurse, while her father worked in the same hospital as an attendant in the psychiatric ward. He later became a bus driver. Berry's parents divorced when she was four years old, and she and her older sister were raised exclusively by their mother. Berry's middle name came from Halle's Department Store, a Cleveland landmark at the time. Berry's name was legally changed to Halle Maria Berry when she was five.
Berry witnessed her alcoholic father frequently beating her mother, and Berry became estranged from him during childhood. Berry was bullied as a child, and learned how to fight and protect herself. She grew up in Oakwood, Ohio, and graduated from Bedford High School, where she was a cheerleader, honor student, editor of the school newspaper, and prom queen. She worked in the children's department of Higbee's department store and attended Cuyahoga Community College. In 1985, she won the Miss Teen All American beauty pageant. In 1986, she won Miss Ohio USA, was the first runner-up at Miss USA, and became the first African-American to represent the United States at the Miss World
grok_lead: Halle Maria Berry (born August 14, 1966) is an American actress and producer of mixed African-American and European descent, born in Cleveland, Ohio, to a Black hospital attendant father and a white psychiatric nurse mother. Raised primarily by her mother after her parents' divorce, Berry entered modeling and beauty pageants in her early twenties, placing as first runner-up in the Miss USA competition. She transitioned to acting in the late 1980s with television roles before achieving film breakthroughs in Jungle Fever (1991) and Boomerang (1992), establishing herself as a leading actress in both dramatic and action genres. Berry's most significant achievement came in 2002 when she became the first African-American woman to win the Academy Award for Best Actress for her role as Leticia Musgrove in the drama Monster's Ball, a performance noted for its raw emotional intensity amid the film's exploration of racial and class dynamics. She gained further prominence portraying Storm, the weather-controlling mutant, in the X-Men film franchise starting in 2000, contributing to its box-office success while showcasing her versatility in superhero action. Other notable roles include the titular character in Catwoman (2004), which received critical backlash and a Razzie Award for Worst Actress despite commercial interest in her physical portrayal. Beyond acting, Berry has produced projects and advocated for health issues like diabetes management, drawing from her own type 1 diagnosis since childhood.
